'''David Whyte Macdonald''' '''CBE FRSE''' (born 1951) is a British [[zoologist]] and [[conservation biologist]]. He first became internationally known for his early research on [[red fox]]es, which led to award-winning documentary films and books, as well as contributions to wildlife conservation policy. He is best known as the founder of the [[Wildlife Conservation Research Unit]] (WildCRU) at the [[University of Oxford]], established in 1986, which he directed for 35 years.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Home |url=https://www.wildcru.org/ |access-date=2025-12-09 |website=WildCRU |language=en-US}}</ref> Macdonald is a [[Senior Research Fellow]] of [[Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford]] with the Title of Distinction of [[Professor]] of Wildlife Conservation at the University of Oxford. He has been an active conservation biologist since graduating from Oxford in 1972, where he earned a [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] (1972), [[Master of Arts (Oxford, Cambridge, and Dublin)|MA]] (1973), [[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] (1977) and [[Doctor of Science|DSc]] (2004).<ref name="oxzoo">{{cite web |year=2010 |title=Professor David Whyte Macdonald |url=http://www.zoo.ox.ac.uk/staff/academics/macdonald_dw.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150227212529/http://www.zoo.ox.ac.uk/people/view/macdonald_dw.htm |archive-date=2015-02-27 |access-date=15 December 2010 |work=Department of Zoology |publisher=[[The University of Oxford]]}}</ref>

== Education and early career ==
Macdonald, the only son of Glaswegian parents, was educated at Wallop Prep School in Surrey, briefly at Emmanuel School in [[Glamorgan]], and then at [[St Lawrence College, Ramsgate|St Lawrence College]] in Kent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=David W. Macdonald {{!}} Author {{!}} LibraryThing |url=https://www.librarything.com/author/macdonalddavidw |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=LibraryThing.com |language=en}}</ref> He read [[zoology]] at [[Wadham College, Oxford]] (1969–72), followed by a DPhil in [[animal behaviour]] in [[Nikolaas Tinbergen|Niko Tinbergen]]’s research group, supervised by [[Hans Kruuk]] and [[H. N. Southern]] (1972–76).<ref name="oxzoo" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-05-13 |title=Oxford scientist named British conservation hero {{!}} University of Oxford |url=https://www.ox.ac.uk/news/2015-05-13-oxford-scientist-named-british-conservation-hero |access-date=2025-12-09 |website=www.ox.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref> He subsequently became a [[Junior Research Fellowship|Junior Research Fellow]] at [[Balliol College, Oxford]] (1976–79), following his father W. A. F. Macdonald (medicine, 1946–53). He served as the Ernest Cook Research Fellow (1979–84) and the Nuffield Research Fellow (1984–87) in the [[Department of Zoology, University of Oxford|Department of Zoology]] at Oxford, before his appointment as Senior Research Fellow in Wildlife Conservation at Lady Margaret Hall in 1986.<ref name=":0" />

==Career==
Macdonald’s research philosophy has been to conduct original biological research that directly informs practical wildlife conservation and environmental management, thereby shaping policy and public debate on conservation issues.<ref name="oxzoo"/> While his early work focused on [[red fox]]es, he has maintained a lifelong emphasis on [[carnivore]]s, increasingly on [[Felidae|felids]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Acclaimed zoologist David Macdonald to grace Fairway Galle Lit Fest 2017 {{!}} Daily FT |url=https://www.ft.lk/entertainment-art/acclaimed-zoologist-david-macdonald-to-grace-fairway-galle-lit-fest-2017/10405-584785 |access-date=2025-12-09 |website=www.ft.lk |language=English}}</ref>

He has published more than 1,500 papers in [[peer-reviewed journal]]s. His most highly cited paper is "The ecology of carnivore social behaviour", published in [[Nature (journal)|''Nature'']] in 1983.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Macdonald |first=David W. |date=1983 |title=The ecology of carnivore social behaviour |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/301379a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=301 |issue=5899 |pages=379–384 |doi=10.1038/301379a0 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He has written or edited more than two dozen books; recent works include ''A Very Short Introduction to Biodiversity Conservation'' (2023) and ''The Badgers of Wytham Woods: A Model for Behaviour, Ecology and Evolution'' (2022).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor David Macdonald named as global finalist for lifetime Award for Conservation Excellence |url=https://www.biology.ox.ac.uk/article/professor-david-macdonald-named-as-global-finalist-for-lifetime-award-for-conservation-excel |access-date=2025-12-09 |website=www.biology.ox.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>

Although centred on carnivores, his research spans an unusually broad range of taxa, including mammals from 11 orders, as well as [[birds]], [[reptile]]s, [[amphibian]]s, [[fish]], [[Butterfly|butterflies]], [[moth]]s and other [[invertebrate]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Linnean Medal 2025 awarded to wildlife biologist Professor David Macdonald |url=https://www.biology.ox.ac.uk/article/linnean-medal-2025-awarded-to-wildlife-biologist-professor-david-macdonald |access-date=2025-12-09 |website=www.biology.ox.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref> His fieldwork has taken place in eight European, nine African, twelve Asian and six South American countries, and covers major themes in [[biodiversity]] conservation such as [[human–wildlife conflict]], [[predator]] management, [[hunting]], [[wildlife disease]], [[epizootiology]], [[wildlife trade]], [[Conservation biology|conservation geopolitics]], [[landscape planning]], [[invasive species]], financial mechanisms, legislation, [[animal welfare]] and conservation ethics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. David Macdonald |url=https://futurefornature.org/guest_of_honour/prof-david-macdonald/ |access-date=2025-12-09 |website=Future For Nature |language=en-US}}</ref>

His recent focus includes the Connecting Landscapes Decision Support System, designed to integrate biodiversity conservation with [[economic development]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-12-06 |title=The best, of Zoology and Entomology, the country has to offer |url=https://www.ru.ac.za/latestnews/archives/2015/thebestofzoologyandentomologythecountryhastooffer.html |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=www.ru.ac.za |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2015 he was listed among the top three individuals in the BBC [[BBC Wildlife|''Wildlife'']] Power List for those likely to make the greatest impact on wildlife in the coming decade. In 2023 he was named one of the two most productive conservation authors globally over the previous 20 years in human–wildlife conflict.<ref>{{cite web |title=Earthwatch Europe – Board and Governance |url=http://www.earthwatch.org/europe/aboutus/staff/board/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101009092306/http://www.earthwatch.org/europe/aboutus/staff/board |archive-date=9 October 2010 |access-date=15 December 2010 |publisher=Earthwatch}}</ref>

== Public understanding of science ==
Macdonald has been active in communicating biology and conservation to the public through films and books. His [[BBC Two|BBC2]] documentary ''Night of the Fox'' introduced broadcast-quality infrared filming and was a finalist for the [[British Academy Film Awards|BAFTA]] Best Documentary Award in 1976. The accompanying book ''Running with the Fox'' won the Natural World Book of the Year Award in 1987.<ref name="Jen Rivett">{{cite news |author=Jen Rivett |date=14 June 2010 |title=University wildlife expert gets CBE for his work |url=http://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/8218316.University/ |access-date=23 May 2012 |newspaper=Oxford Mail}}</ref>

His [[BBC One|BBC1]] film ''Meerkats United'' won the 1988 [[Wildscreen Festival|Wildscreen]] Award and, in a 1996 public vote, was named the "Best Natural History Film Ever Made". Its sequel, ''One for All, All for One'', produced for [[National Geographic]] Explorer, was a finalist at the 1989 [[Animal Behavior Society]] Film Festival.<ref>{{Cite news |title=A wild idea about paying for conservation |url=https://www.economist.com/science-and-technology/2017/08/03/a-wild-idea-about-paying-for-conservation |access-date=2025-12-10 |work=The Economist |issn=0013-0613}}</ref> His seven-part BBC series ''The Velvet Claw'' (1992) explored the natural history of carnivores and was published as a companion book.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Naish |first=Darren |title=Homage to The Velvet Claw, again |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/blog/tetrapod-zoology/homage-to-the-velvet-claw-again/ |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=Scientific American |language=en}}</ref>

The first edition of his ''Encyclopaedia of Mammals'' (1984) sold about 500,000 copies, and the 2009 third edition is widely used as a reference work.<ref>{{Cite web |title=What is 'Just Conservation' ? |url=https://www.oxfordmartin.ox.ac.uk/blog/what-is-just-conservation |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=Oxford Martin School |language=en}}</ref> His children’s book ''Vulpina: The Story of a Fox'' (1977) received positive reviews, and his travel book ''Expedition to Borneo'' (1982) was reissued in 2007. His general-interest books have been translated into multiple European and Asian languages. His research in Southeast Asia also informed the educational computer game ''Unseen Empire''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Fox {{!}} The Sun Magazine |url=https://www.thesunmagazine.org/articles/21318-the-fox |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=www.thesunmagazine.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-10-13 |title=TripAdvisor to work with WildCRU on new wildlife tourism education portal {{!}} University of Oxford |url=https://www.ox.ac.uk/news/2016-10-13-tripadvisor-work-wildcru-new-wildlife-tourism-education-portal |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=www.ox.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>

== Public service ==
In the United Kingdom, Macdonald has served on the boards of [[English Nature]] and [[Natural England]], where he was the founding Chair of the Science Advisory Committee.<ref name=":0" /> He chaired the UK government’s [[Darwin Initiative|Darwin Advisory Committee]] for a decade, and was founding Chair of the [[IUCN]]/[[Species Survival Commission|SSC]] [[Canidae|Canid]] Specialist Group for 25 years, becoming an Emeritus Fellow in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Species 7* |url=https://portals.iucn.org/library/sites/library/files/documents/SSC-Species-044-En.pdf |website=IUCN}}</ref> He has served on the boards of numerous conservation organisations including [[WWF-UK]] (Emeritus Fellow), [[Fauna and Flora International|Fauna & Flora International]], the [[Zoological Society of London]] (Vice President), the [[Wildfowl & Wetlands Trust]], the [[Royal Society for the Protection of Birds|RSPB]], the [[Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals|RSPCA]] (Vice President) and [[The Wildlife Trusts]] (Vice President). Internationally, he has advised the School of Wildlife Conservation at the [[African Leadership University]] in Kigali.<ref name="oxzoo" />

He is currently Chair of Action for Conservation, Chair of Lion Landscapes (working in [[Kenya]], [[Tanzania]] and the [[United Kingdom|UK]]), and a trustee of [[Chester Zoo]] and the [[Oxfordshire]] Local Nature Partnership.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Palminteri |first=Sue |date=2016-02-18 |title=After Cecil: lion perturbation, conservation, and value to a global society |url=https://wildtech.mongabay.com/2016/02/after-cecil-lion-perturbation-conservation-and-value-to-a-global-society/ |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=Wildtech |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Macdonald’s doctoral thesis, ''The Behavioural Ecology of the Red Fox'', received the T. H. Huxley Prize of the Zoological Society of London in 1978.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Annual Review 2003 |url=https://cms.zsl.org/sites/default/files/2022-10/annual-review-2003-17.pdf |website=ZSL.org}}</ref> He later received the Dawkins Prize in 2005,<ref>{{cite web |title=The Dawkins Prize for Animal Conservation and Welfare |url=http://www.balliol.ox.ac.uk/official/miscellany/dawkins/index.asp |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070912192317/http://www.balliol.ox.ac.uk/official/miscellany/dawkins/index.asp |archive-date=12 September 2007 |access-date=15 December 2010 |work=[[Balliol College]] |publisher=[[The University of Oxford]]}}</ref> the [[C. Hart Merriam Award|Merriam Prize]] in 2006,<ref>{{cite web |title=Merriam Award Committee |url=http://www.mammalsociety.org/committees/indexmerriam.asp |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101125011614/http://mammalsociety.org/committees/indexmerriam.asp |archive-date=25 November 2010 |access-date=16 December 2010 |publisher=[[American Society of Mammalogists|ASM]] |df=dmy}}</ref> [[The Mammal Society|The Mammal Society of Great Britain]]’s Gold Medal in 2007,<ref>{{cite web |title=Bursaries, Prizes and Awards |url=http://www.mammal.org.uk/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=199&Itemid=226 |access-date=16 December 2010 |publisher=[[The Mammal Society]]}}</ref> and the [[Zoological Society of London]]’s [[Silver Medal (Zoological Society of London)|Silver Medal]] in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wayback Machine |url=http://static.zsl.org/files/2010-silver-1159.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120917103823/http://static.zsl.org/files/2010-silver-1159.pdf |archive-date=2012-09-17 |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=static.zsl.org}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor David Macdonald |url=https://rse.org.uk/fellowship/fellow/professor-david-macdonald-8580/ |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=Royal Society of Edinburgh |language=en-GB}}</ref>

He received the joint RSPCA and [[British Society of Animal Science]] award for work on wild animal welfare in 2012 and was elected an Honorary Life Member of the [[American Society of Mammalogists]] in 2019.<ref>{{cite web |date=4 March 2008 |title=New Expertise Strengthens RSE Fellowship |url=http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/rse_press/2008/election2008.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090720223057/http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/rse_press/2008/election2008.pdf |archive-date=20 July 2009 |access-date=16 December 2010 |work=Press release |publisher=[[Royal Society of Edinburgh]]}}</ref> In 2025, he was awarded the [[Linnean Medal]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Announcing the Linnean Society's Medal and Award Recipients 2025 |url=https://www.linnean.org/news/2025/04/09/announcing-the-linnean-societys-medal-and-award-recipients-2025 |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=The Linnean Society |language=en}}</ref>

Macdonald has held visiting and honorary positions at Cornell University, the University of Plymouth, the University of Liverpool, and Imperial College London. He is a Fellow of the [[Royal Geographical Society]], the [[Zoological Society of London]], the [[Royal Society of Biology]], and the [[Linnean Society of London]]. He was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in 2010.<ref name="Jen Rivett" /><ref>{{London Gazette |issue=59446 |date=12 June 2010 |page=8 |supp=y}}</ref>
